June 2022 |time=0:00 |lang=French}} born 28 July 1998) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for [[Paris Basketball]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. Ntilikina stands at {{height|ft=6|in=4}} tall and plays the [[point guard]] position. He was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] as the eighth overall pick during the [[2017 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Ntilikina was born in [[Ixelles]], Belgium, on 28 July 1998, to [[Rwanda]]n parents.{{cite web|last=Givony|first=Jonathan|title=FIBA Europe U18 Championship Scouting Reports: Point Guards|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-Europe-U18-Championship-Scouting-Reports-Point-Guards-5197/|website=DraftExpress.com|access-date=13 June 2017|date=4 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818155236/https://www.draftexpress.com/article/FIBA-Europe-U18-Championship-Scouting-Reports-Point-Guards-5197/|archive-date=18 August 2017|url-status=dead}} His mother, Jacqueline Mukarugema, had fled Rwanda with his two brothers because of the [[Rwandan Civil War]] and settled in Belgium a few years before his birth.{{cite web |last1=Begley |first1=Ian |title='The sky's the limit' for NBA draft mystery man Frank Ntilikina |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19697587/nba-draft-2017-sky-limit-nba-draft-mystery-man-frank-ntilikina |website=ESPN |access-date=16 August 2026 |date=22 June 2017}} Ntilikina moved to [[Strasbourg]], France at age three.{{cite web|last=Keh|first=Andrew|title=Frank Ntilikina, a Top N.B.A. Prospect, Is Learning to Play With Fire|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/01/04/sports/basketball/frank-ntilikina-sig-strasbourg-france.html|website=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=13 June 2017|date=4 January 2017}} He subsequently holds both French and Rwandan citizenship.[https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/211764-frank-ntilikina Frank Ntilikina] at fiba.basketball He began his youth club career at the age of five, playing for St-Joseph Strasbourg, before making the move to [[Strasbourg IG]]'s youth academy when he was 15.{{Cite web|title = F. Ntilikina: Deuxième parrain de Have A Basket !|url = http://haveabasket.com/2015/09/06/f-ntilikina-deuxieme-parrain-de-have-a-basket/|website = Have a Basket|access-date = 5 February 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160206084037/http://haveabasket.com/2015/09/06/f-ntilikina-deuxieme-parrain-de-have-a-basket/|archive-date = 6 February 2016|url-status = dead}} Ntilikina participated Evaluations: Guards and Wings| website = draftexpress.com| access-date = 28 February 2016}} ==Professional career== ===SIG Strasbourg (2015–2017)=== Ntilikina spent the majority of the 2014–15 season with the Strasbourg IG youth team, helping them win the French Youth League Championship.{{Cite web|title = Frank Ntilikina|url = http://sigstrasbourg.fr/player/frank-ntilikina/|website = sigstrasbourg.fr|date = 3 April 2015|access-date = 5 February 2016|archive-date = 29 September 2020|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200929003337/https://sigstrasbourg.fr/player/frank-ntilikina|url-status = dead}} He made his debut for the SIG senior team on 4 April 2015 in a French [[LNB Pro A]] [[2014–15 Pro A season|2014–15 season]] contest against [[SOMB Boulogne-sur-Mer|Boulogne-sur-Mer]], seeing 15 minutes of action.{{Cite web|title = Strasbourg / Boulogne-sur-Mer – 27ème journée – 2014/15 – Résultat match – Pro A – LNB.fr|url = http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200009/Resultat-match/8974/resultat-match|website = lnb.fr|access-date = 5 February 2016}} On 15 October 2015, Ntilikina logged his first [[EuroLeague]] minutes, scoring one point in 12 minutes and 16 seconds of play against [[KK Crvena zvezda]].{{Cite web|title = Crvena Zvezda Telekom Belgrade vs. Strasbourg – Game|url = http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=2&seasoncode=E2015#!boxscore|website = euroleague.net|access-date = 5 February 2016}} In December 2015, he signed a four-year contract with SIG Strasbourg.{{Cite web|title = Frank Ntilikina signe un contrat de trois ans|url = http://sigstrasbourg.fr/2015/12/frank-ntilikina-signe-un-contrat-trois-ans/|website = sigstrasbourg.fr|access-date = 5 February 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160206101415/http://sigstrasbourg.fr/2015/12/frank-ntilikina-signe-un-contrat-trois-ans/|archive-date = 6 February 2016|url-status = dead}} He saw the court in 32 contests during the [[2015–16 Pro A season]], averaging 1.2 points per game and earning the [[LNB Pro A Best Young Player]] award.{{Cite web|url=http://basket-ballworld.fr/pro-a-frank-ntilikina-elu-meilleur-jeune-du-championnat/|title=Pro A : Frank Ntilikina élu meilleur jeune du championnat – Basket-BallWorld|date=30 April 2016|website=Basket-BallWorld|language=fr-FR|access-date=3 May 2016|archive-date=18 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190718185345/https://basket-ballworld.fr/pro-a-frank-ntilikina-elu-meilleur-jeune-du-championnat/|url-status=dead}} In the 2016–17 season, Ntilikina became a key part of the Strasbourg team, as he appeared in 45 games for the team while averaging 7.2 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 2.1 assists in 19.3 minutes per game. His successful campaign led him to winning his second straight Pro A Best Young Player award.{{cn|date=October 2025}} In April 2017, Ntilikina entered his name into the [[2017 NBA draft]]. By NBA draft's entry deadline on 12 June, he became one of only 10 international underclassmen to remain in the NBA draft that year. Ntilikina also became one of 20 invitees for the green room on draft night. The night before the draft, Ntilikina played game 4 in the LNB Pro A Finals with SIG Strasbourg before traveling to [[Brooklyn]], New York to participate in the draft personally. After that night, he played his last game with SIG Strasbourg with them losing the LNB Pro A Finals to [[Élan Chalon]].{{Cite web |last=Winfield |first=Kristian |date=22 June 2017 |title=Frank Ntilikina's schedule will make you tired just reading it |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2017/6/22/15856890/frank-ntilikina-nba-draft-travel-knicks-workout |access-date=9 August 2023 |website=sbnation.com}} ===New York Knicks (2017–2021)=== [[File:Brooklyn Nets vs NY Knicks 2018-10-03 td 172a - 1st Quarter.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Ntilikina with the [[New York Knicks]] in 2018]] During the build-up to the [[2017 NBA draft]], there was heavy speculation that the [[Dallas Mavericks]] would select Ntilikina with the ninth overall pick. Mavericks owner [[Mark Cuban]] was quoted as saying that the Mavericks wanted a "pass-first point guard" and said "We can maybe go a little bit more for a project",{{Cite web |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-may-closing-frenchman-frank-ntilikina-no-9-overall-pick-nba-draft/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=22 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190718185345/https://www.mavs.com/mavs-may-closing-frenchman-frank-ntilikina-no-9-overall-pick-nba-draft/ |archive-date=18 July 2019 |url-status=dead }} both of which Ntilikina fit the bill for. When the Knicks ended taking Ntilikina with the eighth pick, the Mavericks chose point guard [[Dennis Smith Jr.]] Ntilikina was also rumoured to be coveted by the Knicks' front office and coaching staff, with whom he met in person.{{cite tweet|number=877568435143680000|user=IanBegley|title=Frank Ntilikina says he met with the...|date=21 June 2017}} On 22 June 2017, Ntilikina was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] with the eighth pick in the 2017 NBA draft.{{cite web |last=Ballow |first=Jonah |date=22 June 2017 |title=Knicks Select Frank Ntilikina with the No. 8 Overall Pick in 2017 |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-select-frank-ntilikina-no-8-overall-pick-2017 |access-date=18 July 2017 |website=NBA.com}} On 5 July, Ntilikina signed with the Knicks.{{cite web |last=Ballow |first=Jonah |date=5 July 2017 |title=Knicks Sign Frank Ntilikina |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-sign-frank-ntilikina |access-date=18 July 2017 |work=NBA.com}} He was the second-youngest active player in the NBA during his rookie year behind [[Ike Anigbogu]].{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Josh |date=11 December 2017 |title=Knicks' Frank Ntilikina includes Lonzo Ball among 'very talented point guards' |url=https://bullswire.usatoday.com/2017/12/11/frank-ntilikina-lonzo-ball-lakers-knicks-nba |access-date=9 August 2023 |website=USA Today}} Ntilikina made his NBA debut on 19 October 2017, in a 105–84 loss to the [[2017–18 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400974441|title=Knicks vs. Thunder – Box Score|publisher=ESPN|date=19 October 2017|access-date=28 April 2018}} He scored his first points on 28 October against the [[2017–18 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]] in a 107–86 win. He recorded nine points, two rebounds, five assists and a steal during the Knicks' home opener.{{Cite news |last=Berman |first=Marc |date=27 October 2017 |title=Porzingis, Ntilikina propel Knicks past Nets for 1st win of season |work=New York Post |url=https://nypost.com/2017/10/27/porzingis-ntilikina-propel-knicks-past-nets-for-1st-win-of-season |access-date=28 October 2017}} On 15 January 2018, Ntilikina recorded his first [[double-double]] with 10 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds, two blocks and a steal in a 119–104 win over the Brooklyn Nets.{{Cite news |last=Kerber |first=Fred |date=15 January 2018 |title=Ntilikina's breakout game shows Knicks what's been missing |work=New York Post |url=https://nypost.com/2018/01/15/ntilikinas-breakout-game-shows-knicks-whats-been-missing |access-date=16 January 2018}} On 24 January 2018, he was selected to represent Team World for the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] during the [[2018 NBA All-Star Game|2018 NBA All-Star Weekend]].{{cite web|title=Ntilikina selected for Rising Stars Challenge|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/knicks-frank-ntilikina-rising-stars-challenge-o37667|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125012837/https://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/knicks-frank-ntilikina-rising-stars-challenge-1.16336143|url-status=live|archive-date=25 January 2018|website=Newsday}} His rookie season in New York was considered by many as underwhelming, and he was often claimed to be a [[draft bust]].{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2018/10/31/frank-ntilikina-beginning-to-silence-any-bust-talk/|title=Frank Ntilikina beginning to silence any bust talk|last=Vaccaro|first=Mike|date=1 November 2018|website=New York Post|access-date=1 April 2019}} Ntilkina was limited to 43 games in his second season due to injuries. Heading into his third season, Ntilikina was coming off a strong performance in the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]]. In the early part of the season, he took over starting point guard duties and began to show great signs of defense. On 23 November 2019, Ntilikina racked up six steals in a 111–104 loss to [[2019–20 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite magazine |last=Vertsberger |first=David |date=24 November 2019 |title=Frank Ntilikina displays switchability vs Spurs |url=https://www.si.com/nba/knicks/news/ntilikina-spurs |access-date=2 January 2020 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}} However, like his previous two seasons, he struggled to shoot the ball and eventually was demoted in favor of [[Elfrid Payton (basketball)|Elfrid Payton]].{{cite web |title=Frank Ntilikina's demotion makes his Knicks future more confusing |url=https://nypost.com/2019/12/24/frank-ntilikinas-demotion-makes-his-knicks-future-more-confusing |last=Berman |first=Marc |website=New York Post |access-date=2 January 2020 |date=24 December 2019}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2021–2023)=== [[File:Frank Ntilikina Dec21.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Ntilikina with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in 2021]] On 16 September 2021, Ntilikina signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks add guard Ntilikina to fill up roster|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-add-guard-ntilikina-to-fill-up-roster/|website=Mavs.com|date=16 September 2021|access-date=16 September 2021}} He made his debut on 21 October 2021, in a 87–113 loss to the [[2021–22 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]], playing four minutes.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401358777|title=Young, Hawks open season with 113–87 rout of Mavericks|date=21 October 2021|publisher=ESPN|access-date=21 October 2021}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2023–2024)=== On 5 August 2023, Ntilikina signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign Frank Ntilikina|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-frank-ntilikina|website=NBA.com|date=5 August 2023|access-date=5 August 2023}} On 8 February 2024, Ntilikina was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive James Bouknight, Frank Ntilikina And Ish Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-james-bouknight-frank-ntilikina-and-ish-smith|website=NBA.com|date=8 February 2024|access-date=8 February 2024}} ===Partizan (2024–2025)=== On 20 June 2024, Ntilikina signed a two-year contract with [[KK Partizan]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS), [[ABA League]] and [[EuroLeague]].{{cite news|title=Frank Entilikina je novi košarkaš crno-belih|url=https://partizan.basketball/vesti/aktuelno/3735|work=partizan.basketball|date=20 June 2024|access-date=21 June 2024|language=Serbian}}{{cite news |title=Frank Ntilikina returns to Europe, joins Partizan {{!}} EuroLeague |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/frank-ntilikina-returns-to-europe-joins-kk-partizan/ |access-date=2 October 2025 |work=Euroleague Basketball |date=20 June 2024}} He helped Partizan win the [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|2024–25 ABA League championship]] and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|2024–25 Serbian League championship]]. In 29 ABA League games, he averaged 7.1 points, 1.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game, and in 21 EuroLeague games, he averaged 7.0 points, 1.7 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Frank Ntilikina, Basketball Player, News, Stats - Eurobasket |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Frank-Ntilikina/332228 |website=Eurobasket LLC |access-date=2 October 2025 |url-access=subscription}} On 1 September 2025, it was reported that Ntilikina had extended his deal with Partizan until 2027,{{cite news |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro |title=Partizan's Frank Ntilikina reportedly extends deal until 2027 with reduced salary |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/partizans-frank-ntilikina-reportedly-extends-deal-until-2027-with-reduced-salary/ |access-date=2 October 2025 |work=Sportando |date=1 September 2025}} but he ultimately parted ways with the team later that month.{{cite news |last1=Hill |first1=Arthur |title=Frank Ntilikina Joins Olympiacos |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/09/frank-ntilikina-will-reportedly-be-moved-to-olympiacos.html |access-date=2 October 2025 |work=hoopsrumors.com |date=26 September 2025}} ===Olympiacos (2025–2026)=== On 26 September 2025, Ntilikina signed a contract with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] (GBL) and EuroLeague.{{cite news |last1=Γραβιά |first1=Τζένη |title=Παίκτης του Θρύλου ο Ντιλικίνα! |url=https://www.olympiacosbc.gr/el/news-el/announcements-el/11484-1-8.html |access-date=2 October 2025 |work=Olympiacos BC |date=26 September 2025 |language=el-gr}} During his stint with Olympiacos, he won the [[2025–26 EuroLeague]] title as well as the Greek League championship. ===Paris Basketball (2026–present)=== On August 12, 2026, Ntilikina signed with [[Paris Basketball]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Frank Ntilikina joins Paris|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/frank-ntilikina-joins-paris-basketball/|date=August 12, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|access-date=August 12, 2026}} ==National team career== Ntilikina averaged 7.4 points, 2.0 assists, 1.6 rebounds and one steal per game, en route to winning the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] with the Under-16 French junior national team.{{Cite web|title = Perfect France Beat Hosts, Lift Title|url = web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2016/France|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902182147/http://www.fiba.basketball/europe/u18/2016/France|url-status=live|archive-date=2
